title: Ordinary native pullback comparison preserves finite evaluation
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, any morphism f:X→Y of schemes and any ordinary coefficient-system module M on Y, let κ be the left-adjoint uniqueness comparison from pullbackTensorSequenceInverse to native VaryingRing.pull, obtained from integralNativeOrdinaryDirectIso and the specified ordinary adjunctions [lem-sf-integral-native-direct-comparison]. At every n, evaluation of κ followed by native moduleEvalG [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] and openSquarePullbackModel [def-trf-finite-pullback-coordinate-comparison] equals the composite of pullbackTensorSequenceInverseEvaluation inverse with pullbackTensorLevelIntrinsic [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. All maps are the specified unit-normalized comparisons, with no properness or open-immersion hypothesis.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve evaluation and adjunction units/counits; primitive whole-system operation comparison in Step 1 of lem-sf-integral-support-strict-tower-comparison. Stacks 03DI, 0941, 0D6E; Zheng Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10.

proof.text: Use the existing integralNativeOrdinaryDirectIso and the identity-on-sections theorem for compactSupportOrdinaryDirectEvaluation. Uniqueness of pullbackTensorSequenceDirectEvaluation identifies the composite ordinary direct-image evaluation square with its prescribed comparison. No derived direct-image comparison theorem is used.

Prove a generic comparison-of-mates identity using the Hom equivalence, unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app and unit_mateEquiv_symm. The native moduleEvalG unit normalization identifies its inverse mate. The intrinsic pullback comparison and the ordinary inverse-evaluation normalization identify the inverse mate of the original direct square. The finite pullback coordinate comparison preserves units. The generic identity therefore compares ordinaryPullIso, native moduleEvalG and the original ordinary evaluation.

proof_origin.place: U3: normalized ordinary mates and exact localization, the inverse-image step in the native open comparison. This helper is fully proved, isolated to keep each module below the 60-second compile limit.

theorem integralNativeOrdinaryPullEvaluation {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ)
    (M : coefficientSequenceModules l E Y) :
    (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n).map
      ((((pullbackTensorSequenceAdjunction l E f).ofNatIsoRight
      (integralNativeOrdinaryDirectIso l E f)).leftAdjointUniq
        (ProEtale.VaryingRing.moduleAdj (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
          (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) f)).hom.app M) ≫
      (ProEtale.VaryingRing.moduleEvalG (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
        (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) f n).hom.app M ≫
      (openSquarePullbackModel (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) f).hom.app
        ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).obj M) =
      ((pullbackTensorSequenceInverseEvaluation l E f n).symm ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _ (pullbackTensorLevelIntrinsic l E f n)).hom.app M
